items.title: Phil Woods interviewed by Monk Rowe, Delaware Water Gap, PA, November 8, 1999
items.q: Chuck Andrews on bass, he was with Woody Herman’s band when Nat Pierce was the piano player

ctx.x: Well at what point in all this musical activity did you decide, or did you decide, that you were going to make a career out of jazz playing? Was it a conscious decision or did it kind of just fall in your lap?

I wanted to be a musician, and I kind of fell into the studio thing. I could always jam, I mean Springfield, Massachusetts back in those days, we had a little bebop band with Sal Salvador, the guitar player with Kenton, Joe Morello, who became Brubeck’s drummer, the famous “Take Five” solo is Joe Morello. Chuck Andrews on bass, he was with Woody Herman’s band when Nat Pierce was the piano player, and who am I leaving out, oh Hal Serra, a very fine piano player. And Al Bryant on trumpet, who I think maybe he’s…

the — I mean we play classical but— even though I was a clarinet major, I was still the guy that played the alto sax. Everybody knows who you are in a school situation. And there’s the lounge lizards and then there’s the beboppers and all that. But it turned out that, not competing, but being around all these other kids, I found out I was better than I thought I was. I mean I could play the piano. A lot of the violin players couldn’t play the piano. I mean I can play a little Bebop Bud Powell, but it served me…

items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: Interviewer introduces Phil Woods as a subject of a previous interview; Interviewee responds with 'All right.' indicating acknowledgment but no personal interaction described.

ctx.x: And the one thing he's forgetting about completely is that there are really many, many exceptional young players who do develop. And if there isn't a gig, they will make a gig, which was really the way it started. And it's really the way Mr. Woods started, and he was a very good educa-
tor, and he was one of the first people to be involved at the high school level, of teaching kids at that age.
